root.name: Van Geet Opening: Pfeiffer Gambit
root.moves: 1. Nc3 d5 2. f4 d4 3. Ne4 e5

overview: White pushes f4 against Black's ...d4 and ...e5, and after 4.Nf3 Black can take on f4 (the Sleipnir Countergambit line). White is aiming for development and kingside play for the pawn on f4, while Black has a central pawn chain and an easy extra pawn. It is rare and read from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Nf3 and d3 or e3 to develop quickly against the e5 and d4 pawns
Win back material or hit the centre with fxe5

black_ideas.idea: Hold the e5 pawn or take f4 and consolidate
Use the d4 and e5 pawns to cramp White's pieces

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d4 and e5, White pawn on f4 under pressure

character.notes: Both centres are in flux and White has given material for activity.

gambit.notes: The f4 pawn can be taken by Black, who keeps the pawn.

soundness.notes: White falls behind in the centre and has only a time lead as compensation.

structure.notes: Quick pawn exchanges and piece play dominate rather than a fixed chain.

approach.notes: A little-known side line of an already rare opening.

level.notes: Dubious, so not Beginner, and little theory exists.

sublines_that_differ.name: Sleipnir Countergambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. Nc3 d5 2. f4 d4 3. Ne4 e5 4. Nf3
sublines_that_differ.how: The most played continuation; White develops and lets Black take on f4.
